verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतच्छ्रुत्वा महाराज धृतराष्ट्रोम्बिकासुतः । शोकस्यान्तमपश्यन्वै हतं मेने सुयोधनम् ॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard this (the above intelligence), the great king Dhritarashtra, the son of Ambika, experienced, indeed, the farthest limit of grief and considered Suyodhana slain (in the battle); and highly perturbed, he fell down upon the ground, like an elephant, that had lost all his senses.
verses.bhavadeepa: पीडयित्वा हत्वेत्यनेककर्तृकेऽपि क्त्वाप्रत्ययश्छान्दसः अन्येऽभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते इति वनिवन्तं वा शब्दद्वयं दृशिग्रहणादाद्ये तुगपि । पीडयन् निघ्नन्निति वाऽर्थः ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: विह्वलः पतितो भूमौ नष्टचेता इव द्विपः । तस्मिन्निपतिते भूमौ विह्वले राजसत्तमे ॥२॥
verses.english: As soon as the king fell down, the illustrious Vidura also, O king, afflicted with sorrow for the king's distress, fell down on Earth.

verses.sanskrit: आर्तनादो महानासीत् स्त्रीणां भरतसत्तम । स शब्दः पृथिवीं कृत्स्नां पूरयामास सर्वशः ॥३॥
verses.english: O the most excellent of the Bharata race, on the fall of the highly agitated and foremost of monarchs upon the ground, there was tremendous wailing of women.

verses.sanskrit: शोकार्णवे महाघोरे निमग्ना भरतस्त्रियः । रुरुदुर्दुःखशोकार्ता भृशमुद्विग्नचेतसः ॥४॥
verses.english: Which (the noise) filled the entire earth to all its points. The ladies of the house hold of Bharata, greatly burnt in grief and with hearts filled with great anxiety, bewailed most bitterly, plunged as they were in the very deep ocean of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: राजानं च समासाद्य गान्धारी भरतर्षभ । निःसंज्ञा पतिता भूमौ सर्वाण्यन्तःपुराणि च ॥५॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race advancing towards the king, Gandhari, as well as all other ladies of the royal household, fell down upon the ground, all having lost their senses. a

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ताः सञ्जयो राजन्समाश्वासयदातुराः । मुह्यमानाः सुबहुशो मुञ्चन्त्यो वारि नेत्रजम् ॥६॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O monarch, Sanjaya consoled those ladies, who were highly oppressed with sorrow and deprived of their senses and who, again, were copiously shedding tears from their eyes.

verses.sanskrit: समाश्वस्तास्त्रियस्तास्तु वेपमाना मुहुर्मुहुः । कदल्य इव वातेन धूयमानाः समन्ततः ॥७॥
verses.english: In spite of their being comforted (by Sanjaya), those ladies shivered every moment like the plantain tree constantly shaken by the wind.

verses.sanskrit: राजानं विदुरश्चापि प्रज्ञाचक्षुषमीश्वरम् । आश्वासयामास तदा सिञ्चन्स्तोयेन कौरवम् ॥८॥
verses.english: Thereupon Vidura, too, began to sprinkle water over the face of that descendant of Kuru and consoled that powerful monarch, who had eyes of wisdom.

verses.sanskrit: स लब्ध्वा शनकैः संज्ञां ताश्च दृष्ट्वा स्त्रियो नृपः । उन्मत्त इव राजेन्द्र स्थितस्तूष्णीं विशाम्पते ॥९॥
verses.english: O Lord of carth, having gradually attained to consciousness and understanding the rniserable plight of those ladies, the monarch, like at senseless being, remained silent for sometime.

verses.sanskrit: ततो ध्यात्वा चिरं कालं निःश्वस्य च पुनः पुनः । स्वान् पुत्रान् गर्हयामास बहु मेने च पाण्डवान् ॥१०॥
verses.english: Thereupon he, reflecting (upon the matter) for a pretty long time and sighing heavily and incessantly, condemned his own sons but spoke highly of the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: गर्हयंश्चात्मनो बुद्धिं शकुनेः सौबलस्य च । ध्यात्वा तु सुचिरं कालं वेपमानो मुहुर्मुहुः ॥११॥
verses.english: Then having condemned his own reason as well as that of Shakuni the son of Subala and meditated (upon the matter) for a long while, the king trembled at every moment.

verses.sanskrit: संस्तभ्य च मनो भूयो राजा धैर्यसमन्वितः । पुनर्गावल्गणिं सूतं पर्यपृच्छत सञ्जयम् ॥१२॥
verses.english: The king had, again, restrained his mind and collected enough of patience. Then he asked his charioteer Sanjaya, the son of

verses.sanskrit: यत्त्वया कथितं वाक्यं श्रुतं सञ्जय तन्मया । कच्चिद्दुर्योधनः सूत न गतो वै यमक्षयम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, whatever words were uttered by you were all heard by me. O charioteer, has not my son Duryodhana gone to the region of Yama? Has my son, who is ever desirous of victory, grown desperate of success? O Sanjaya, do you repeat to me in detail truly what you have said already.

verses.sanskrit: जये निराशः पुत्रो मे सततं जयकामुकः । ब्रूहि सञ्जय तत्त्वेन पुनरुक्तां कथामिमाम् ॥१४॥
एवमुक्तोऽब्रवीत्सुतो राजानं जनमेजय । हतो वैकर्तनो राजन्सह पुत्रैर्महारथः ॥१५॥
verses.english: O Janamejaya, having been thus asked, the Suta addressed the king, saying-"O king, the son of Vikartan., that mighty car-warrior, was killed in battle along with his sons and brothers, as well as the other warrior sons of Suta, who were all great bowmen and who also were ready to give up their lives in battle.
verses.bhavadeepa: जये इति । इष्टवियोगमात्रेण दशरथादिर्मृतः । अस्य तु जये नैराश्यमधिकं मरणकारणमस्तीति भावः । उक्तां संक्षेपेण । पुनर्ब्रूहि विस्तरेण ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातृभिश्च महेष्वासैः सूतपुत्रैस्तनुत्यजैः । दुःशासनश्च निहतः पाण्डवेन यशस्विना । पीतं च रुधिरं कोपाद्भीमसेनेन संयुगे ॥१६॥
verses.english: Dusshasana, too, was slain in an encounter by Bhimasena, that famous son of Pandu, who had drunk his (Dusshasana's) blood out of anger.
